Directly age-standardised rates, with Fay-Feuer gamma intervals

Source: R/indigenous.R
agestd.Rd

The rate a population would have with the age structure of a standard population, for one or more groups, with Fay and Feuer's gamma confidence interval.

Usage

agestd(events, pop, std, grp = NULL, per = 1e+05, conflvl = 0.95)

Arguments

events, pop

Numbers of events and of people, one per age group (and group).

std

The standard population, one count per age group (its shares are the weights).

grp

Optional labels: one rate per group, each over the same age groups in the same order.

per

Rate per this many people (default 100,000).

conflvl

Confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A data frame with group, events, rate, lower, upper, and the attributes var (the variances, on the per-person scale) for rategap.

Details

With \(d_i\) events and \(n_i\) people in age group \(i\) and standard weights \(w_i\) (the standard population's shares), the rate is \(y = \sum w_i d_i / n_i\), its variance \(v = \sum (w_i / n_i)^2 d_i\), and with \(w_M = \max_i w_i / n_i\) the limits are \(\frac{v}{2y} \chi^2_{2y^2/v}(\alpha/2)\) and \(\frac{v + w_M^2}{2(y + w_M)} \chi^2_{2(y + w_M)^2/(v + w_M^2)}(1 - \alpha/2)\) (Fay and Feuer 1997). The interval is conservative (coverage at least nominal in Fay and Feuer's simulations) and reduces to the exact Garwood interval for a single age group: suited to the few events of small communities. With no events the lower limit is 0. Rates are per per people. Age groups are matched to std by position: order the rows of each group by age, in the order of std.

The choice of standard matters: Statistics Canada's comparisons of First Nations, Metis and Inuit mortality standardise to the Indigenous population's own age structure (Kumar and Tjepkema 2019), which is younger than Canada's.

References

Fay MP, Feuer EJ (1997). Confidence intervals for directly standardized rates: a method based on the gamma distribution. Statistics in Medicine 16(7):791-801.
doi:10.1002/(sici)1097-0258(19970415)16:7<791::aid-sim500>3.0.co;2-#

Kumar MB, Tjepkema M (2019). Suicide among First Nations people, Metis and Inuit (2011-2016): Findings from the 2011 Canadian Census Health and Environment Cohort (CanCHEC). Statistics Canada 99-011-X2019001.

See also

rategap.

Examples

# made-up counts for one small community, by five age groups, to show the computation
std <- c(30000, 25000, 20000, 15000, 10000)   # a younger standard population
agestd(events = c(4, 9, 11, 6, 3), pop = c(9000, 8000, 6000, 4000,
                                                           2000),
                std = std)
#>   group events    rate    lower    upper
#> 1   all     33 115.625 79.23967 165.0186
